topic: How a hash table finds your data in one step
hooks: Your computer finds one name among a billion in a single step.
Why doesn't a search through a billion names take forever?
One line of maths makes lookups instant.
titles: How Hash Tables Find Data in One Step

scenes.narration: Your computer finds one name among a billion in a single step. How?
Checking every name one by one would take ages, even for a fast machine.
A hash function turns each name into a number, and that number is the address of a bucket.
In Python, a dictionary does this for you every time you look up a key.
The surprise is that collisions are expected, so good tables keep buckets short and grow before they fill up.
Where else could turning data into an address save time?

closing_question: Where else could turning data into an address save time?
